channel.title: FixMyError.net – Recently Added Errors
channel.description: Newly added developer and infrastructure error fixes on FixMyError.net.

item.title: (Mix) You're trying to run :my_app on Elixir v1.15.7 but it has declared
item.description: The elixir: requirement in mix.exs (for example "~> 1.17") does not match the Elixir on your PATH. It works on your laptop and fails in CI or a container because the two have different Elixir installs, often an asdf or mise .tool-versions file that the build image ignores. Remember Elixir and OTP…

item.title: /usr/bin/env: 'python': No such file or directory
item.description: The script's shebang asks for a command called python, and current Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and macOS releases only ship python3. Python 3 is installed; there is just no executable with the bare name. It also catches scripts saved with Windows line endings, where env looks for 'python\r' and the…

item.title: AAPT: error: resource android:attr/lStar not found
item.description: android:attr/lStar was added in API 31, and a dependency (usually androidx.core 1.7 or newer, pulled in transitively) references it. Your compileSdk is older than 31, so the build tools cannot find the attribute. It looks like a broken library but is a version mismatch, and it commonly appears…

item.title: Android Gradle plugin requires Java 17 to run. You are currently using Java 11
item.description: AGP 8 needs JDK 17 to run Gradle itself, separate from the Java version your app code targets. Android Studio bundles a suitable JDK, which is why the build works in the IDE and fails on the command line or in CI, where JAVA_HOME still points at Java 11. Raising sourceCompatibility does nothing…

item.title: Android: Namespace not specified. Specify a namespace in the module's build file
item.description: Android Gradle Plugin 8 stopped reading the package attribute from AndroidManifest.xml and requires namespace in build.gradle instead. Your own module is easy to fix; the harder case is an old third-party library or Flutter or React Native plugin that has not been updated, which fails the build…

item.title: AWS Load Balancer Controller: couldn't auto-discover subnets
item.description: The controller builds an ALB by finding subnets tagged for load balancers, and none in the cluster's VPC carry the tag. Public ALBs need kubernetes.io/role/elb=1 and internal ones kubernetes.io/role/internal-elb=1. eksctl tags subnets it creates, so this usually appears on clusters built with…

item.title: bash: ulimit: open files: cannot modify limit: Operation not permitted
item.description: An unprivileged shell can lower its soft limit or raise it up to the hard limit, but never past the hard limit. Running ulimit -n 65535 asks for more than the hard limit your session inherited. Editing limits.conf does nothing for services, which take their limits from systemd, and only applies to…

item.title: C++: error: invalid use of incomplete type 'class Foo'
item.description: The compiler has seen a forward declaration of Foo but not its definition, and this line needs the full layout: calling a member, taking sizeof, holding it by value or deleting it. Headers often forward-declare on purpose to cut compile times, so the fix is to include the real header in the .cpp…

item.title: Celery: Received unregistered task of type 'myapp.tasks.send_email'
item.description: The worker took a message off the queue but has never imported the module that defines the task, so it has no idea what to run. The producer and the worker disagree about the task's name or code: the worker was started with a different -A app, autodiscovery missed the module, the task was renamed…

item.title: cert-manager: Failed to determine a valid solver configuration
item.description: None of the solvers on the Issuer matches the domains being requested, so cert-manager has no way to attempt a challenge. Solvers can be limited with a selector by dnsNames, dnsZones or labels, and a new hostname, a wildcard needing DNS01 while only HTTP01 is configured, or an Ingress pointing at…

item.title: CMake Error: Compatibility with CMake < 3.5 has been removed from CMake.
item.description: CMake 4.0 dropped support for projects that declare cmake_minimum_required below 3.5. The code is unchanged; your CMake upgraded, often silently through Homebrew, pip or a CI image, and an old project or vendored dependency still says VERSION 2.8 or 3.1. Usually the fix belongs upstream, and in…

item.title: CPU0: Core temperature above threshold, cpu clock throttled
item.description: The CPU hit its thermal limit and the hardware cut its clock speed to cool down. Everything still works, just slower, so it shows up as a benchmark or build that is fast for a minute and then degrades, or a server that is slower in summer. The cause is physical more often than not: clogged fans…

item.title: Discord API: 50013 Missing Permissions
item.description: The bot is in the server but lacks a permission for this action in this place. Discord evaluates role permissions and then channel overwrites, so a role can grant Send Messages server-wide while one channel denies it. Moderation actions add role hierarchy on top: a bot cannot kick, ban or change…

item.title: dnsmasq: failed to create listening socket for port 53: Address already in use
item.description: Something else already owns port 53. On Ubuntu and Fedora that is almost always the systemd-resolved stub listener on 127.0.0.53, and on desktops it can be a second dnsmasq started by NetworkManager or libvirt. Because dnsmasq binds the wildcard address by default, it collides even though the…

item.title: Ecto: could not lookup Ecto repo MyApp.Repo because it was not started
item.description: Ecto found the repo module but no running process registered under it. The code is fine; it is running somewhere the application tree has not been started: a Mix task, a release eval command, a seeds script run with plain elixir, or an ExUnit test helper that skipped…

item.title: Elixir: function :crypto.hmac/3 is undefined or private
item.description: OTP 24 removed the old crypto API, so :crypto.hmac/3 no longer exists. Your own code rarely calls it directly: the usual culprit is an old version of a dependency (an outdated plug_crypto, a JWT or AWS signing library) that still does. The project compiled fine on OTP 23, which is why it breaks…

item.title: GraphQL: Field "user" of type "User" must have a selection of subfields
item.description: The field returns an object type, and GraphQL never returns a whole object implicitly: you have to name the scalar fields you want inside braces. The reverse mistake, adding braces to a scalar or enum field, gives a matching "must not have a selection" error. It tends to appear after a schema…

item.title: GraphQL: Unknown argument "first" on field "Query.users"
item.description: Validation rejected the query before any resolver ran because the schema has no argument with that name on that field. It is often a client written against a different schema version, a Relay-style first/after query sent to a server that paginates with limit/offset, or a field that takes its…

item.title: INFO: task kworker blocked for more than 120 seconds
item.description: The hung task detector found a process stuck in uninterruptible sleep (D state) for two minutes, almost always waiting on I/O. The task it names is the victim, not the cause: look at the storage behind it. Typical culprits are an NFS or iSCSI server that went away, a saturated or failing disk, or…

item.title: Kafka: The coordinator is not available (COORDINATOR_NOT_AVAILABLE)
item.description: Consumer groups and transactions need the internal __consumer_offsets topic, and the broker cannot find a healthy leader for the partition that owns your group. On a fresh single-broker dev cluster the classic cause is offsets.topic.replication.factor left at its default of 3, so the topic can…

item.title: Kubernetes Ingress Controller Fake Certificate served instead of yours
item.description: ingress-nginx serves its built-in self-signed certificate whenever it cannot match the request to a usable TLS secret. The secret may be missing or in a different namespace from the Ingress, the hostname in spec.tls may not match spec.rules, or the client is not sending SNI at all. cert-manager…

item.title: LeakSanitizer: detected memory leaks
item.description: LeakSanitizer runs when the process exits and reports heap blocks that nothing points to any more. It is on by default with AddressSanitizer on Linux, which is why it starts failing tests the day someone enables -fsanitize=address. Direct leaks are the ones to fix first; indirect leaks are usually…

item.title: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
item.description: The kernel tracks every connection passing through netfilter, and that table has a fixed size. Once it fills, new connections are silently dropped, which looks like random timeouts under load rather than an error. It is common on busy load balancers, NAT gateways and Kubernetes nodes where…

item.title: nginx: no resolver defined to resolve backend.example.com
item.description: When proxy_pass contains a variable, nginx resolves the hostname at request time instead of at startup, and that needs its own resolver directive: it does not read /etc/resolv.conf. People add the variable on purpose so nginx starts even when the backend is down, or so it picks up DNS changes…

item.title: nginx: SSL_do_handshake() failed while SSL handshaking to upstream
item.description: nginx reached the HTTPS backend but the TLS handshake failed, and the usual reason surprises people: nginx does not send SNI to upstreams by default. A backend behind a CDN, a cloud load balancer or any shared host picks its certificate by SNI, so without it the handshake is refused with a…

item.title: RabbitMQ: ACCESS_REFUSED - Login was refused using authentication mechanism
item.description: The broker rejected the username and password, but the credentials are not always what is wrong. The default guest user is restricted to localhost, so guest/guest works on your machine and fails from another container or host. The other common causes are a user with no permissions on the virtual…

item.title: S3: SlowDown: Please reduce your request rate (503)
item.description: S3 is throttling requests to one key prefix, not your whole account. Each prefix supports around 3,500 writes and 5,500 reads a second, and a burst that lands on a single prefix (every object under logs/2026-10-17/, say) hits that ceiling while the rest of the bucket is idle. It also appears…

item.title: S3: The requested bucket name is not available (BucketAlreadyExists)
item.description: Bucket names are global across every AWS account in a partition, so somebody else already owns this one, possibly years ago. BucketAlreadyOwnedByYou is the friendlier variant and means you created it yourself, usually in another region or an earlier Terraform run. A name deleted recently can also…

item.title: Slack API: not_in_channel
item.description: The bot token is valid and has chat:write, but the app has not been added to the channel it is posting to. Slack treats that as membership, not permission, so adding more scopes will not help. It often shows up when a webhook-style integration moves to chat.postMessage, or when the channel ID in…

item.title: Squid: ERR_ACCESS_DENIED Access control configuration prevents your request
item.description: The request reached Squid and Squid itself refused it: the destination site is fine. Squid walks http_access rules top to bottom and the first match wins, so a client network missing from localnet, a CONNECT to a port outside SSL_ports, or a new allow rule placed below http_access deny all will…

item.title: Structure needs cleaning
item.description: This is EUCLEAN, the kernel saying the filesystem found corrupt metadata and refused to trust it. On XFS and ext4 it usually follows an unclean shutdown, a failing disk or a virtual disk that lost writes. The file or directory named in the error is only where the damage was noticed: the repair has…

item.title: sudo: a terminal is required to read the password
item.description: sudo wanted a password but had no terminal to ask on, because the command ran over ssh without a TTY, from cron, in a CI job or inside an Ansible or Docker step. The same command works when you type it interactively because there you have a terminal and possibly a cached sudo timestamp. The fix is…

item.title: This operation has been blocked as a potential Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
item.description: Apollo Server 4 turns on CSRF prevention by default. It refuses GET requests and "simple" POSTs (form-encoded, multipart or text/plain) unless they carry a header a browser cannot add cross-site without a preflight. Normal JSON clients are unaffected, so it usually bites curl one-liners, health…

item.title: Twilio 21608: Trial accounts cannot send messages to unverified numbers
item.description: The request is fine; the account is still on a trial, and trials may only message numbers verified on that account. It catches teams whose staging works because every developer verified their own phone, then fails the first time a real customer number is used. Upgrading the account removes the…

item.title: Using degraded feature set UDP instead of UDP+EDNS0 for DNS server
item.description: systemd-resolved probes each upstream server for EDNS0 and DNSSEC support and steps down when replies look broken. The upstream is usually a home router or ISP resolver that mangles or drops EDNS0 packets. On its own the message is noise, but if lookups are also slow or failing it means resolved…

item.title: zone example.com/IN: NS 'ns1.example.com' has no address records (A or AAAA)
item.description: The zone lists a name server inside itself but never gives that server an A or AAAA record, so nobody could find it. BIND refuses to load the zone rather than serve a delegation that cannot work. Frequent causes are a typo in the glue name, a missing trailing dot that turned ns1.example.com. into…

item.title: .NET: BinaryFormatter serialization and deserialization have been removed
item.description: .NET 9 removed the BinaryFormatter implementation: the type still compiles, but every call throws PlatformNotSupportedException. It was deprecated because deserialising untrusted data with it allows remote code execution. Code that has not touched it directly often still hits it through an old…

item.title: .NET: NETSDK1045: The current .NET SDK does not support targeting .NET 10.0
item.description: The project's TargetFramework is newer than the SDK doing the build. Installing the new runtime is not enough, you need the matching SDK. The usual surprise is a global.json pinning an older SDK, or a CI image or Visual Studio install that lags behind, so the project builds on one machine and not…

item.title: Airflow: DAG.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'schedule_interval'
item.description: Airflow 3 removed the schedule_interval and timetable arguments that had been deprecated since 2.4; a DAG now takes a single schedule argument. Every DAG file written for Airflow 2 fails to import after the upgrade and shows up as a Broken DAG, even though nothing in the file changed. The same…

item.title: Alertmanager: Notify for alerts failed: notify retry canceled after 16 attempts
item.description: Alertmanager tried to deliver a notification until the group's retry window ran out, and every attempt failed. The line itself only says it gave up; the reason follows it, usually a webhook returning 4xx, a Slack or Teams URL that was revoked, an SMTP relay rejecting the login, or DNS and proxy…

item.title: Ansible: [WARNING]: Platform linux on host web1 is using the discovered Python
item.description: Ansible had to guess which Python to run modules with on the managed host, and warns because a later package install could change the answer. It is harmless on its own, but the same guessing is behind confusing failures elsewhere: a module that says a library is missing when you installed it for a…

item.title: Ansible: Conditionals must have a boolean result
item.description: ansible-core 2.19 rewrote templating and stopped guessing the truthiness of non-boolean values in when, until, failed_when and changed_when. A condition like when: my_var, where my_var holds the string "false" or a list, used to be coerced quietly and sometimes wrongly; now it fails the task…

item.title: Ansible: ERROR! the role 'nginx' was not found in
item.description: Ansible searched its role path and found no directory with that name. The search starts relative to the playbook file, not the directory you run the command from, so moving a playbook into a subfolder breaks roles that sat next to it. Roles from Galaxy also need installing on each machine that…

item.title: ASP.NET Core: Synchronous operations are disallowed. Call ReadAsync or set
item.description: Kestrel and IIS block synchronous reads and writes on the request and response bodies, because a blocked thread per request starves the thread pool under load. The exception usually comes from a library rather than your code: an XmlSerializer, an old Newtonsoft.Json formatter, or a…

item.title: AWS Lambda: Runtime.HandlerNotFound: index.handler is undefined or not exported
item.description: Lambda found and loaded the file named in the handler setting, but that file has no export called handler. The usual causes are a default export instead of a named one, a build step that puts the file in dist/ while the handler setting still says index, or a TypeScript build that was never run so…

item.title: AWS Lambda: Runtime.UserCodeSyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside
item.description: The Node.js runtime decides whether your handler is an ES module or CommonJS from the file extension and the nearest package.json, exactly as Node does locally. An index.js containing import statements is treated as CommonJS unless package.json says "type": "module". Locally a bundler or ts-node…

item.title: Azure Functions: No job functions found. Try making your job classes
item.description: The host started but indexed zero functions, so there is nothing to run. The message talks about public classes, which is a .NET in-process hint, yet the real cause is usually elsewhere: FUNCTIONS_WORKER_RUNTIME not matching the code, a .NET isolated app deployed with the in-process setting, a…

item.title: Cloudflare: cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC
item.description: DYNAMIC means Cloudflare never considered the response for caching, which is different from a MISS. By default Cloudflare only caches static file extensions such as .css, .js and images; HTML and API responses pass straight through however long your Cache-Control max-age is. Adding headers at the…

item.title: Django: CacheKeyWarning: Cache key will cause errors if used with memcached
item.description: Memcached keys must be under 250 bytes and contain no spaces or control characters. Django warns about this on every backend so that code developed against the local memory cache does not break when it reaches a memcached production cluster. The usual culprits are keys built from URLs, search…

item.title: Fluent Bit: Action/metadata line [1] contains an unknown parameter [_type]
item.description: Elasticsearch 8 removed mapping types, and rejects any bulk request that still sends _type. Fluent Bit's es output sent _type: _doc by default, so a pipeline that was working breaks the moment the cluster is upgraded, with every chunk failing as HTTP 400. Every chunk is rejected, so nothing…

item.title: Grafana: Datasource ${DS_PROMETHEUS} was not found
item.description: The dashboard was exported for sharing, which replaces every data source with a placeholder input like ${DS_PROMETHEUS}. The import screen normally asks you to map that input to a real data source, but provisioning, the HTTP API and Terraform skip that step and load the placeholder as if it were a…

item.title: gRPC: CANCELLED (code 1)
item.description: The call was cancelled, almost always by the caller rather than the server. In Go the client context was cancelled (often a deferred cancel() or an HTTP request that ended), in Node and Python the client closed the call or the channel. Seen on the server, it means the client gave up and any…

item.title: gRPC: UNAVAILABLE: DNS resolution failed for service
item.description: The channel could not turn the target into an address. Besides a plain typo, two gRPC quirks cause it: the target string uses its own URI syntax, so a scheme like http:// or a trailing path is read as part of the hostname, and C-core may use the c-ares resolver, which ignores /etc/hosts entries…

item.title: gRPC: UNAVAILABLE: failed to connect to all addresses
item.description: This is the C-core wording (Python, Node's older grpc package, Ruby, C++, PHP) for a channel that resolved its target but could not open a working connection to any of the addresses. The text hides the real cause, which follows it in the debug string: connection refused, a TLS mismatch, a…

item.title: Java: PatternSyntaxException: Dangling meta character '*' near index 0
item.description: A quantifier such as *, + or ? appeared with nothing before it to repeat. It almost never comes from a regex you meant to write: String.split, replaceAll and matches all take a regular expression, so splitting on "+" or "*" as a plain separator fails. The same code works with "," or ";" because…

item.title: JavaScript: Invalid regular expression: Duplicate capture group name
item.description: Reusing a named group in different alternatives, as in (?\d{4})-\d{2}|\d{2}/(?\d{4}), only became legal in ES2025. Chrome 125, Firefox 129 and Safari 17 accept it; older browsers, older Node versions and some bundler parsers throw at the moment the script loads. A pattern that passes every test on…

item.title: libvirt: Cannot access storage file (as uid:107, gid:107): Permission denied
item.description: The system libvirt daemon starts QEMU as an unprivileged user (qemu or libvirt-qemu, uid 107 on many distributions), not as you. That user needs search permission on every directory leading to the disk image, so an image in your home directory fails even when the file itself is world readable. On…

item.title: Loki: error at least one label pair is required per stream
item.description: Loki indexes streams by their labels and will not accept a push whose stream has none. The shipper is configured, but its relabelling dropped every label: commonly a Promtail or Alloy relabel rule with action keep or labeldrop matching too much, or Kubernetes discovery labels that start with __…

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID: AADSTS50076: Due to a configuration change made by your
item.description: A Conditional Access policy requires multi-factor authentication for this sign-in, and the client used a flow that cannot show an MFA prompt: the resource owner password grant, a legacy SMTP or IMAP client, or a script calling with a username and password. Interactive sign-ins from the same…

item.title: Microsoft Entra ID: AADSTS700016: Application with identifier was not found
item.description: The client_id in the request does not exist in the tenant the request was sent to. Usually the app is single tenant and the code points at /common or /organizations, or a user from another organisation is signing in to an app that was never made multi-tenant. Copying the object ID instead of the…

item.title: Next.js: Failed to set Next.js data cache, items over 2MB can not be cached
item.description: The App Router stores fetch() responses in its data cache, and refuses any single response over 2MB. The page still renders, but that fetch runs again on every request, so a page you expected to be static quietly hits your API each time. It usually shows up when an endpoint grows past the limit…

item.title: OAuth 2: {"error":"unsupported_grant_type"}
item.description: The token endpoint did not see a grant_type it accepts. Far more often than a genuinely unsupported grant, the parameter is there but unreadable: OAuth 2 requires the token request as application/x-www-form-urlencoded, and many HTTP clients send a JSON body by default. The server finds no…

item.title: Postfix: 450 4.1.8 Sender address rejected: Domain not found
item.description: The receiving Postfix has reject_unknown_sender_domain enabled and could not find an A or MX record for the domain in your MAIL FROM address. It is a 4xx, so the sender retries and the mail sits in the queue. Common causes are an application sending from an internal name like app.local, a server…

item.title: Prometheus: opening storage failed: lock DB directory: resource temporarily
item.description: Another Prometheus process already holds the lock file in the data directory. Two Prometheus servers must never share a TSDB directory, so this check is protecting your data. It normally means an old process never exited, a second container or systemd unit points at the same volume, or a…

item.title: Python: --- Logging error --- TypeError: not all arguments converted
item.description: The logging module formats messages lazily with the % operator, and a call like logger.info("user", user_id) passes an argument with no %s to put it in. Logging deliberately does not raise: it prints this block to stderr and drops the message, so the program carries on and the log you wanted is…

item.title: sed: -e expression #1, char 15: unknown option to `s'
item.description: sed ended the s command early because the pattern or replacement contained the delimiter, nearly always a / inside a path or URL. Everything after that slash is read as flags, and the first character that is not a valid flag triggers the error. It typically appears when a shell variable is…

item.title: SMTP: 530 5.7.0 Must issue a STARTTLS command first
item.description: The server requires an encrypted session before it will accept AUTH or MAIL FROM, and the client went straight in over plain text. Usually the client is configured for port 25 or 587 with TLS switched off, or it is set to implicit TLS mode on a port that expects STARTTLS. The opposite mismatch…

item.title: SMTP: 550 5.7.25 The IP address sending this message does not have a PTR record
item.description: Gmail checks that the sending IP has reverse DNS, and that the name it points to resolves forward to the same IP. The PTR record lives with whoever owns the IP block, usually your hosting provider, not in your own DNS zone, which is why adding records to your domain changes nothing. New VPS hosts…

item.title: Spark: [CAST_INVALID_INPUT] The value 'abc' of the type "STRING" cannot be cast
item.description: Spark 4.0 turned ANSI SQL mode on by default. A cast that used to quietly return NULL for a malformed value now fails the whole query, and so do integer overflow and division by zero ([DIVIDE_BY_ZERO]). Jobs that ran for years start failing on the first dirty row after the upgrade, and the bad…

item.title: Spark: UnsupportedFileSystemException: No FileSystem for scheme "s3"
item.description: Hadoop does not ship an implementation for the plain s3:// scheme outside Amazon EMR. Open source Spark talks to S3 through the s3a:// connector in the hadoop-aws jar, which is not on the classpath of a stock Spark download. The same path works on EMR or Databricks, which bundle their own S3…

item.title: Vagrant: The IP address configured for the host-only network is not within
item.description: VirtualBox 6.1.28 started restricting host-only networks to 192.168.56.0/21 on Linux and macOS. Vagrantfiles that have used addresses like 10.0.0.10 or 192.168.33.10 for years stop working after a VirtualBox update, and Vagrant passes on the refusal. The address is fine as an address; VirtualBox…

item.title: WSL: HCS_E_HYPERV_NOT_INSTALLED
item.description: WSL 2 runs its distros in a lightweight virtual machine, and Windows could not create it. Either the Virtual Machine Platform feature is off, or hardware virtualisation (Intel VT-x, AMD SVM) is disabled in the firmware. A BIOS update or reset often turns it back off silently, which is why WSL can…

item.title: Apache: AH01071: Got error 'Primary script unknown'
item.description: The message is PHP-FPM's, relayed by Apache: the script path Apache sent over FastCGI does not exist, or cannot be read, from PHP-FPM's point of view. Usually the handler builds the path from the wrong document root, or PHP-FPM runs in a container where the code lives somewhere else. The browser…

item.title: App Store Connect: ITMS-91053: Missing API declaration
item.description: Since May 2024 Apple rejects uploads that call certain "required reason" APIs, such as UserDefaults, file timestamps or system boot time, without a privacy manifest saying why. The call is often in a third-party SDK rather than your code, so updating the dependency to a version that ships its own…

item.title: C++: error: 'format' is not a member of 'std'
item.description: std::format is C++20 and lives in , which needs both the C++20 flag and a recent enough standard library: GCC 13, Clang 17 with libc++, or Visual Studio 2019 16.10. GCC still defaults to C++17, so one build file without the flag is enough. On macOS the deployment target matters as well as the…

item.title: C++: error: 'uint8_t' does not name a type
item.description: The file uses fixed-width integer types without including , and only ever compiled because another standard header pulled it in indirectly. GCC 13 trimmed those internal includes in libstdc++, so code that built for years breaks on upgrade, often inside a third-party library. The same happens with…

item.title: C++: terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
item.description: An allocation asked for more memory than the allocator could provide, nothing caught the exception, and the runtime aborted. On Linux, real memory exhaustion usually brings the OOM killer instead, so this message more often means one absurd request: a negative length converted to size_t, a size…

item.title: Dart: Bad state: No element
item.description: firstWhere, first, last or single ran on a collection with nothing in it, or nothing matching, and these throw a StateError rather than returning null. item.description: Emscripten's runtime hit a fatal condition and called abort(), but release builds leave out assertions to save size, so the reason was thrown away. item.title: ethers v6: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'Web3Provider')
item.description: ethers v6 removed the providers, utils and constants namespaces, so v5 code such as ethers.providers.Web3Provider or ethers.utils.parseEther reads a property of undefined. It usually appears when a fresh npm install pulled v6 into a project or tutorial written for v5. The classes still exist…

item.title: Flutter: Looking up a deactivated widget's ancestor is unsafe
item.description: Code used a BuildContext after its widget had left the tree, almost always after an await: the user navigated away or the dialog closed, then the callback carried on and called Navigator.of(context) or ScaffoldMessenger.of(context). item.title: ingress-nginx: 400 The plain HTTP request was sent to HTTPS port
item.description: The controller is speaking plain HTTP to a backend that only accepts HTTPS, and the backend's own web server answers with this 400. ingress-nginx proxies to pods over HTTP unless told otherwise; it does not guess TLS from a Service port of 443. item.title: Ingress: spec.rules[0].http.paths[0].pathType: Required value
item.description: networking.k8s.io/v1 made pathType mandatory on every path, where the old v1beta1 API filled it in for you. item.title: Proxmox: can't lock file '/var/lock/qemu-server/lock-100.conf' - got timeout
item.description: Another task still holds the lock on that VM's configuration, so the new start, stop or backup waited and gave up. The holder is usually a backup, snapshot or migration that is still running or hung, and killing the wrong process can leave the VM in a half-finished state. Check what holds the lock…

item.title: Python: re.error: global flags not at the start of the expression
item.description: An inline flag such as (?i) or (?s) appears somewhere other than the very start of the pattern. Python 3.6 to 3.10 only warned about it, and 3.11 made it an error, so code that has worked for years breaks on upgrade. It is common when patterns are built by joining strings together, each with its…

item.title: Rails: Missing encryption key to decrypt file with
item.description: Rails found config/credentials.yml.enc but has no key to open it, because config/master.key is git-ignored and RAILS_MASTER_KEY is not set. It works on the developer's laptop that ran rails new and fails on every other machine, CI job and container. Generating a new key does not help: it cannot…

item.title: Redis: MOVED 3999 10.0.0.12:6379
item.description: The node you asked does not own the hash slot for that key and is telling you which node does. A cluster-aware client follows this silently, so seeing it as an error means the client is running in standalone mode against a cluster, for example a plain connection to an ElastiCache or MemoryStore…

item.description: Ruby 3.4 moved csv, base64, bigdecimal and several other libraries out of the default gems and into bundled gems, and Ruby 3.3 warns about each one it sees you require. item.description: Gmail is temporarily deferring mail from your IP or domain because recent volume looks like spam, judged by complaints and sudden changes in sending rate. item.description: Microsoft 365 accepted your username and password but refused the login because authenticated SMTP submission is turned off for the tenant or the mailbox. It is off by default in newer tenants and when security defaults are enabled. The password is not wrong, so resetting it will not help; a…

item.title: SMTP: 550 5.7.1 Client host [203.0.113.5] blocked using zen.spamhaus.org
item.description: The receiving server looked up your sending IP in a DNS blocklist and found it listed, so it rejected the connection before reading the message. Your content and authentication are irrelevant here; the IP's reputation is the problem. Cloud and residential IP ranges are often listed as a whole, so…

item.title: Spark: Container killed by YARN for exceeding memory limits
item.description: YARN measured the whole executor process and killed it for using more physical memory than the container allowed. That is different from a Java heap OutOfMemoryError: the heap may be fine, and the excess is off-heap memory from Python workers, Arrow buffers, netty or native libraries. Raising…

item.description: A task tried to read shuffle output from another executor and that executor was gone, so the stage has to be recomputed. item.title: VirtualBox: VT-x is being used by another hypervisor (VERR_VMX_IN_VMX_ROOT_MODE)
item.description: VT-x is enabled and working, but another hypervisor on a Linux host already owns it, almost always the KVM kernel module. Older VirtualBox releases cannot share VT-x, so the VM refuses to start. It commonly appears after installing an Android emulator, GNOME Boxes or virt-manager, which load KVM…

item.title: Apache: AH01630: client denied by server configuration
item.description: mod_authz_core decided the request was not allowed for that directory, so it never reached the file and the response is a 403 with nothing in the access pattern to explain it. On an upgraded server it is usually a 2.2 style Order and Allow block being ignored, or a new document root that no…

item.title: Apache: Invalid command 'Order', perhaps misspelled or defined by a module
item.description: Order, Allow and Deny moved into mod_access_compat in 2.4, so configuration written for 2.2 no longer parses unless that module is loaded. The same wording appears for any directive whose module is absent, which is why enabling the compatibility module is a stopgap and rewriting the block is the…

item.title: Dart: Bad state: Cannot add new events after calling close
item.description: A closed StreamController still exists, and something is holding the old reference and adding to it. In Flutter it is normally a controller closed in dispose while an async callback completes just afterwards, or a shared service whose controller was closed by the first widget that happened to use…

item.title: dig: ;; Truncated, retrying in TCP mode
item.description: The answer did not fit in the UDP message size the client offered, so the server set the TC bit and the client started again over TCP. The retry normally succeeds, so the visible symptom is a slow lookup, or an intermittent failure wherever a firewall permits port 53 over UDP but not TCP.

item.title: DNS: CNAME and other data (CNAME at the zone apex)
item.description: A name may hold a CNAME or it may hold other record types, never both, so a CNAME on the zone apex collides with the SOA and NS records that have to live there. The zone then fails to load, and hosted providers report it as an invalid record rather than as an error in the file.

item.title: DNS: REFUSED
item.description: The server answered and declined to do the work, which is what separates this from a timeout or NXDOMAIN. In practice it is a recursive resolver that does not serve your client address, or an authoritative server being asked about a zone it does not host, which is common once a split horizon setup…

item.title: Emscripten: Cannot call unknown function (make sure it is exported)
item.description: ccall and cwrap look the symbol up in the module at runtime, and the linker had already removed it because no C code referenced it. That is why it appears in optimised builds and not in debug ones: at -O2 dead code elimination drops any function only ever called from JavaScript.

item.title: Error 1053: The service did not respond to the start or control request
item.description: A service has about 30 seconds to report back to the service control manager, and the process either failed before doing so or spent that time on startup work. A console application installed as a service never reports at all, which is why it runs perfectly from a command prompt and times out as a…

item.title: First requests after a deploy are slow, then it settles
item.description: A freshly started process serves unoptimised code until the JIT has enough samples, with empty connection pools, empty caches and a cold page cache underneath. Rolling the deployment moves the slow requests around rather than removing them, so the graph looks like the load balancer picking bad…

item.title: Flutter: Incorrect use of ParentDataWidget
item.description: Expanded, Flexible and Positioned only mean something to one kind of parent, and the tree has one of them under something else, usually because a Container or a Padding was inserted between it and the Row. The message names both the widget and the ancestor it actually found, and the layout beneath…

item.title: Flutter: MissingPluginException: No implementation found for method
item.description: The Dart half of a plugin is present and the native half was never registered, so the method channel has nothing on the other end. A hot restart after adding the dependency is the usual cause, because plugin registration happens when the app is built and installed rather than when Dart reloads.

item.title: Flutter: Waiting for another flutter command to release the startup lock
item.description: The SDK takes a file lock while it updates its own caches, and a command killed part way through leaves that lock file behind. Nothing holds it any more, so the wait never ends, and clearing one file inside the SDK directory is all that is needed.

item.title: Homebrew: Cannot install under Rosetta 2 in ARM default prefix
item.description: The arm64 Homebrew in /opt/homebrew refuses to run in a translated process, which is what happens when the terminal itself was opened with Rosetta or a shell inherited an x86_64 environment. Two installations can coexist, one per prefix, so the message is really about which one the current shell…

item.title: JVM: pause with no GC in the log (long time to safepoint)
item.description: A safepoint stops every application thread, and the pause includes however long the slowest thread takes to reach one, which is not counted as collection time. A counted loop over a large array or a thread inside a long JNI call can hold the rest of the JVM for hundreds of milliseconds while the…

item.title: Latency spikes with khugepaged and compaction in the profile
item.description: Transparent huge pages let the kernel back a mapping with 2MB pages, but once memory is fragmented the faulting thread has to compact before it gets one, and it waits while that happens. The result is a tail latency spike on a machine with plenty of free memory, usually on a large heap process…

item.title: ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture arm64
item.description: Compilation succeeded and the linker could not find a definition for something that was declared, so the reference survived to the link step. The architecture in the message is a red herring most of the time: a source file missing from the target, a library built for the other slice, or a C header…

item.title: macOS: "App" is damaged and can’t be opened. You should move it to the Bin
item.description: Gatekeeper is reporting a failed signature or notarisation check on a quarantined download, not a corrupted file. An app unzipped by a tool that dropped part of the bundle, modified after signing, or fetched from a mirror that never notarised it all end here, and the wording sends people to…

item.title: Name resolves with dig but not from the application
item.description: dig talks to a server directly, while the application goes through the stub resolver on 127.0.0.53, which keeps its own per link servers, search domains and cache. The two disagree after a VPN connects, when a container inherits the host resolv.conf, or while a negative answer is still cached.

item.title: nginx: [emerg] a duplicate default server for 0.0.0.0:443
item.description: Only one server block per listening address may carry default_server, and nginx refuses to start rather than choose. It nearly always follows a second site being enabled while it still has the packaged default configuration flag, or a sites-enabled directory holding two symlinks to the same file.

item.title: nginx: 1024 worker_connections are not enough
item.description: Each worker has a fixed number of connection slots and a proxied request uses two of them, one to the client and one to the upstream, so the ceiling arrives at roughly half the concurrency you expected.
